title: a passing release dry run ends on what it could not predict, with no verdict line, and its rows 6 and 7 name HEAD as the commit the cut would tag
body:
## Problem

hv ran `bin/devbin release v0.1.9 --dry-run` on 2026-10-06 and read it as a failure: "I don't think it worked". It had passed, at rc 0: steps 1, 2 and 5 done, 3, 4 and 6 to 9 `would`, 10 and 11 skipped, and no FAILED row. Three things in what it prints point the other way, and one of them is wrong.

1. **No verdict.** A cut ends `release: <tag> is released.` (lib/cmd/release:1057). A dry run ends at :1038-1043: the table, then, when anything went unreached, `release: NOT REACHED by this dry run, so not predicted:` and its list, then `return 0`. So the last words of a passing dry run are "NOT REACHED" and "not predicted", and a pass differs from a failure only by an exit status the person does not see and a FAILED row that is absent.
2. **"resume with".** The header (:500) reads `release: v0.1.9 (DRY RUN: ...) -- resume with: bin/devbin release v0.1.9` on every run. Resume is what a stopped cut says; after a dry run, the next command is the cut itself.
3. **Rows 6 and 7 name HEAD as the tag's commit, and a cut whose step 4 commits never tags HEAD.** `commit` is `release_commit`'s answer (:498), which is HEAD while no tag exists (lib/release.steps:173), and only the real cut's step 4 moves it to the commit it makes (:688). A dry run leaves it at HEAD, so row 6 asks `before: tag v0.1.9 at 58d837acf3ae` and row 7 reads `annotated tag v0.1.9 at 58d837acf3ae` (:787, :822). The cut tagged d7f2ed13, the commit its step 4 made on a HEAD four commits later, and on the same HEAD it would still have tagged a new commit. The sha is right only where step 4 reads `already` or the run resumes a tag.

The same `commit` reaches two more lines. Row 11 (:1009), for a project that declares `ci.query`, prints the same `${commit:0:12}` under a dry run. And step 6 reads each remote with `release_read_remote "$commit" push`, so under a dry run whose step 4 would commit, a remote already holding HEAD reads as holding the release commit, and the plan drops the commit half. Measured by dc on 2026-10-08, on main 9f21eb3d with 0185 v2.1, with releasecut.bats's `cut_project`, whose origin holds HEAD: the dry run's row 6 reads `ask before: tag v1.0.1 at da668768c966; push tag to origin` and row 8 `origin tag`, where the cut on the same shape tagged the commit its step 4 made and pushed `commit tag`. devbin pushes main before a cut, so this is the common case.

## Measured

hv's dry run of v0.1.9, 2026-10-06, on HEAD 58d837acf3ae, as hv pasted it (rows 1 to 4 and 8 to 11 cut here):

```
  5  gates       done        3 gate(s) passed on HEAD 58d837acf3ae in place -- a dry run makes no release commit, so this predicts the gates rather than gating the release
  6  confirm     would       ask before: tag v0.1.9 at 58d837acf3ae; push commit tag to local; push commit tag to upstream
  7  tag         would       annotated tag v0.1.9 at 58d837acf3ae, its message the notes body

release: NOT REACHED by this dry run, so not predicted:
  - step 6's confirmation: a dry run never asks
```

Row 5 says what HEAD is, and rows 6 and 7 then present it as the tag's commit. AT-4.6 (tests/unit/releasecut.bats:406) asserts each step's state and "NOT REACHED by this dry run", and nothing about how the run ends or which commit rows 6 and 7 name. Read at main fe4bffca, whose lib/cmd/release is d7f2ed13's.

## Fix

1. A dry run ends with one verdict line after the NOT REACHED list, saying that no step failed and where the cut would stop to ask: eg `release: dry run of v0.1.9 -- no step failed; the cut stops to ask at step 6`. The wording is the builder's, and the arms hold the fact. A dry run that fails already ends at its FAILED row, at exit 1, and is unchanged.
2. Under a dry run, the header names the cut as the next command, not a resume.
3. Where step 4 reads `would`, rows 6, 7 and 11 name the tag's commit as the release commit step 4 makes on HEAD, never as HEAD's sha, and step 6 reads each remote as one the release commit is still to be made on top of HEAD, as the pre-flight reads it under `preflight-new`: a remote at HEAD lacks it, so the plan pushes the commit and the tag, and a remote moved past HEAD is refused. Where step 4 reads `already`, or the run resumes a tag, the sha is the tag's and stays, and so does the plan.
4. docs/releasing.md:18 says how a dry run ends.

## Done when

1. A passing dry run's last line is its verdict, at exit 0, and a failing one still ends at its FAILED row, at exit 1. The verdict arm is red on d7f2ed13 first.
2. With step 4 `would`, none of rows 6, 7 and 11 reads `at <HEAD's sha>`, red on d7f2ed13 first; with HEAD already carrying the stamp, all three still name HEAD's sha, the control. With origin at HEAD, the dry run's push plan, rows 6 and 8, carries the commit half, red on d7f2ed13 first; with HEAD already the release commit it is `commit tag`, and `tag` alone once main is pushed, the controls; and a remote moved past HEAD is refused.
3. A dry run's header does not read "resume with", and a stopped cut's still does.

When filed, the Problem, Fix and Done when named rows 6 and 7 only. Row 11 and the push plan were added at review, on vc's rulings of 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-08 on dc's readings, being the same cause: under a dry run whose step 4 would commit, `commit` is HEAD.

## Resolution

Landed at f52f4d92 on a green full suite (vc's, 2273 of 2273 ok, 0 not ok, .errors empty, seal 20261008-0906).

1. A dry run that passes ends with one verdict line, after the list of what it could not reach: `release: dry run of v0.1.9 -- no step failed; the cut stops to ask at step 6`. The line names the tag. Its tail says what the cut does at step 6: it stops to ask, or, given `--yes`, `the cut does not stop to ask`, or, for a release with nothing left, `the cut has nothing left to ask about`. Given `--yes`, the dry run's row 6 reads `--yes given: ...` in the words the cut's own row uses, since step 6 now builds them once for both, and step 6's confirmation is no longer listed as unpredicted, since `--yes` answers it. A dry run that fails is unchanged: it stops at its FAILED row and the stopped line, exit 1, and prints no verdict.
2. Under a dry run the header names the cut as the command that releases for real, `-- cut with: bin/devbin release v<version>`. A cut, stopped or not, still says `-- resume with:`.
3. Where a dry run's step 4 reads `would`, there is no release commit yet, and `commit` is still HEAD, which the cut never tags: its step 4 makes a new commit on HEAD. Rows 6, 7 and 11 now name `the release commit step 4 makes` instead of HEAD's sha, and row 5 still names HEAD, which is what the gates ran on. Where step 4 reads `already`, or the run resumes a tag, the rows name the release commit's sha as before, HEAD moved on or not.
4. The push plan had the same cause. Step 6 read each remote against `commit`, so under such a dry run a remote at HEAD read as holding the release commit, and rows 6 and 8 planned `tag` where the cut pushes `commit tag`. A remote at HEAD is the usual case when main is pushed before a cut. Step 6 now reads with `push-new`, a mode of `release_read_remote` shaped like `preflight-new`: <commit> is HEAD and the release commit is still to be made on top of it, so a remote at HEAD lacks it and the plan carries the commit half; a remote moved past HEAD is refused, as pre-flight refuses one; and the pending detail is in halves, as under `push`. One reading covers both `-new` modes, so under `preflight-new` a remote at HEAD lacks the release commit too. Pre-flight reads only whether a remote is refused, and a `-new` answer is never `already` while the tag is absent, so nothing it prints changes.
5. docs/releasing.md, lib/pages/release.md and docs/configuration.md say how a dry run ends, what its header names, what its row 6 says given `--yes`, and how, where step 4 would make the release commit, it names that commit and plans its push.

The arms, in releasecut.bats, all ten carrying 0181 in their titles:

- A passing dry run's last line is its verdict, after the NOT REACHED list.
- The verdict's two other tails: a dry run given `--yes`, whose row 6 says `--yes given:` of the commit step 4 makes and which lists no unpredicted confirmation; then the cut given `--yes`, whose own row 6 says the same of the commit it made; then that finished release run again, with nothing left.
- A failing dry run, its gate exiting 4, stops at step 5 at exit 1, its last line the stop and no verdict anywhere, and its header names the cut.
- A dry run's header is the whole line naming the cut, with no `resume with`; the control is a cut stopped at step 6, which still names the resume.
- With step 4 `would`, rows 6 and 7 carry no part of HEAD's sha and name the commit step 4 makes, while row 5 names HEAD.
- With step 4 `would` and origin at HEAD, the fixture's own state and asserted as such, rows 6 and 8 plan `commit tag`.
- The control for both: a cut stopped at step 6 names, in its own question, the release commit its step 4 made; a dry run then names that commit's sha in rows 6 and 7 with a plan of `commit tag`; once main is pushed, `tag` alone.
- With `ci.query` declared, row 11 names the commit step 4 makes and carries no part of HEAD's sha; once the release commit exists, its sha; and once the release is cut, the tag on that commit, and HEAD has moved on, a dry run resuming the tag still names the tagged commit, never HEAD.
- The verdict names the tag where the tag differs from the target and from `v<version>`: `--patch --dry-run` under the tag template `{version}`, whose verdict names `1.0.1`, neither `--patch` nor `v1.0.1`.
- A remote that moves past HEAD while the gates run, the probe gate pushing a later commit to origin and fetching it, is refused at step 6 under `push-new`, naming the later commit, as pre-flight refuses one found there; the dry run prints no verdict.

`last_line` is a new helper in releasecut.bats, the last line of the output that is not blank. `row_of`, one row of the table whole, is in tests/lib/release_fixtures.bash as the one home of the row predicate, and `state_of` now reads its state through it, passing a failure of `row_of`'s on, so an arm that reads a row's state and its detail reads them from the same line. releasecut.bats's header, which still said steps 6 to 11 were WP-05 and WP-06 and that a cut passing step 5 stopped there with exit 3, now says what the file holds: the cut, steps 1 to 11, with --dry-run and --yes.

Evidence, in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-dc/0181/runs/. The build is 95dbeef7 in a scratch clone: main 476cf82e, with batch 3 landed, then cc's 0186 v1.1 and 0187 v1.1 patches by `git am`, the bytes batch 4 landed, then 0181's four commits; v1.1, 184b28f9, adds the header's comment to them, and nothing else, so the runs below, on v1, hold for it. 0181 is stacked on 0186, as vc ruled for the two that share lib/cmd/release and releasecut.bats; 0187 shares no path with it. 0186 changes only pre-flight's tmp/ check in lib/cmd/release, and 0181's diff on it is its diff on 0185 v2.1 alone, hunk headers aside.

- Red on d7f2ed13 first, its release code under the build's two test files, whose 0181 arms are the stack's byte for byte, under BSD tools and with GNU tools first on PATH (red-d7f2ed13-{bsd,gnu}-20261008-073618.log, and again with the build's own copies, red-d7f2ed13-{bsd,gnu}-20261008-082405.log, whose failure lines are the same). Every arm but the control, which passes, is red at the assertion it is aimed at on that code, read from its failure line, and no helper is missing. The verdict arm fails at its last line; the tails at row 6's `--yes given:`; the failing dry run and the header at the header; the rows at `row 6 names HEAD's sha`; the push plan at `row 6 does not plan the commit's push`; row 11 at its words; the tag arm at the verdict; and the refusal at an exit of 0.
- The build was made in four commits; the first two run as variants and read as aimed. The first, the fix less the push plan, turns only the push-plan arm, the refusal and the `--yes` row red. The second, before critic-shell's first round, turns only the `--yes` row red.
- Mutants, 26, each applied once and parsed, run with the fix, d7f2ed13's code and the first two commits under both tool sets on the build before its rebase, 0181 alone on main with 0185 v2.1, whose diff is this one: 60 of 60 sections as aimed (var-20261008-073716/), and each mutant's failure line read against the assertion it is aimed at, not only its arm. The mutants: the verdict dropped; printed before the NOT REACHED list; printed by a failing dry run too; naming the target, and naming `v` and the version, rather than the tag; the `--yes` tail and the nothing-left tail each lost; given `--yes`, the confirmation still listed as unpredicted, and row 6 saying `ask before`; the cut's own `--yes` row given words of its own; a dry run's header saying `resume with`, and every header saying `cut with`; rows 6, 7 and 11 each naming `commit`'s sha; the commit's name set before step 4, and read from HEAD; the commit never and always read as still to be made; step 6 never and always reading with `push-new`; and in the reader, a remote at HEAD read as holding the commit under a `-new` mode, `push-new` not refusing a remote moved past HEAD, its detail in `status`'s words rather than halves, and each `-new` mode dropped from the one reading in turn. The last of those, `preflight-new` dropped, turns the existing pre-flight arm for a remote moved past HEAD red. Four mutants also redden the arm for the `--yes` and nothing-left tails, each at a line that names what they broke: row 6 naming `commit`'s sha, at the dry run's `--yes` row; the commit always read as still to be made, and its name set before step 4, at the cut's own `--yes` row; and `push-new` always, at the finished release's row 6, since a remote at the tag's commit then reads as lacking it.
- The targeted run (releasecut, releasecore, releasestatus and release, with helpers, contract, neutral, documentation, readonlygit, harness and help), on 95dbeef7 with its tree clean before and after: under BSD tools 529 of 529 (targeted-bsd-20261008-082604.log, 08:26:04Z to 08:38:35Z), and with GNU tools first on PATH 529 of 529 (targeted-gnu-20261008-083835.log, 08:38:35Z to 08:51:07Z). Two in each are harness.bats arms whose subject is `require_command`'s own skip, and they skip as they expect.
- The patch is `git diff` from the tree beneath 0181, which is main's code once batch 4 landed, to v1.1 at 184b28f9. It is v1's patch, which was byte for byte the one cut on 0186 alone before the rebase, plus the header's hunk. Applied on a fresh clone of main, every one of its seven files is v1.1's bytes, and outside intent/ that tree is v1.1's.
- critic-shell reviewed the build twice and found no defect in the code on any path it traced. Round 1 found no critical and no warning, three recommendations, and six places in the docs and comments that said more than the code did. Round 2 found no critical and no warning, four recommendations and four notes. Both are folded in:
  - the cut's own question and a resumed tag's row 11 are held;
  - the verdict is asserted where the tag differs from the target and from `v<version>`;
  - the row predicate has one home;
  - step 6 joins the work left once and builds the `--yes` words once;
  - the `--yes` tail says the cut does not stop to ask;
  - row 11's arm checks that the tag is on the release commit;
  - the docs and comments carry their conditions and say only what the code does.

Declared limits:

- `no step failed` speaks for the steps a dry run reaches; the NOT REACHED list above it names what it did not predict.
- The refusal arm moves the remote from inside a gate, which is the one place a test can put a remote's move between pre-flight's read and step 6's. No arm moves one between step 6 and step 8, and none needs to: a dry run pushes nothing.
